extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent owners, third-party petitioners, patent examiners, and counsel handling post-grant proceedings in the United States
extracted.subtask_short: inter partes and post‑grant review rules
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory requirements, thresholds, timing, procedures, and effects governing inter partes review (IPR), pre‑AIA inter partes reexamination, and post‑grant review in the U.S. patent system. Includes petition content, institution standards, conduct rules, amendment and estoppel rules, appeals, and certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an inter partes review (35 U.S.C. 311(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the provisions of this chapter, a person who is not the owner of a patent may file with the Office a petition to institute an inter partes review of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR scope — grounds and prior art limitations (35 U.S.C. 311(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner in an inter partes review may request to cancel as unpatentable 1 or more claims of a patent only on a ground that could be raised under section 102 or 103 and only on the basis of prior art consisting of patents or printed publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadline for IPR petitions (35 U.S.C. 311(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for inter partes review shall be filed after the later of either (1) the date that is 9 months after the grant of a patent; or (2) if a post-grant review is instituted under chapter 32, the date of the termination of such post-grant review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOTE: Pursuant to Public Law 112-274, Jan. 14, 2013, the filing deadlines of subsection (c) do not apply to patents not subject to the first inventor-to-file provisions of the AIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition requirements — fee, parties, claims, grounds, evidence (35 U.S.C. 312(a)(1)-(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition filed under section 311 may be considered only if: (1) accompanied by the fee; (2) identifies all real parties in interest; (3) identifies, in writing and with particularity, each claim challenged, the grounds for the challenge, and the evidence supporting the grounds, including copies of patents/printed publications and affidavits/declarations if relying on expert opinion; (4) provides other information as Director may require; and (5) provides copies of required documents to the patent owner or its representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of cited patents/printed publications and supporting affidavits/declarations must be included; petitioner must serve required documents on patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of petitions (35 U.S.C. 312(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as practicable after receipt of a petition under section 311, the Director shall make the petition available to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution threshold — reasonable likelihood (35 U.S.C. 314(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may not authorize an inter partes review unless the information presented in the petition and any response shows there is a reasonable likelihood that the petitioner would prevail with respect to at least one of the claims challenged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the statutory threshold for instituting review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for institution decision (35 U.S.C. 314(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall determine whether to institute an inter partes review within 3 months after receiving a preliminary response to the petition or, if no preliminary response is filed, the last date on which such response may be filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of institution and commencement date (35 U.S.C. 314(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall notify the petitioner and patent owner in writing of the determination whether to institute and shall make such notice publicly available; notice includes the date on which the review shall commence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑appealability of institution decision (35 U.S.C. 314(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination by the Director whether to institute an inter partes review under this section shall be final and nonappealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner preliminary response right (35 U.S.C. 313)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an inter partes review petition is filed under section 311, the patent owner has the right to file a preliminary response within a time period set by the Director setting forth reasons why no inter partes review should be instituted based on failure to meet any requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to civil actions — pre‑filing bar (35 U.S.C. 315(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: An inter partes review may not be instituted if, before the date the petition is filed, the petitioner or real party in interest filed a civil action challenging the validity of a claim of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to civil actions — automatic stay (35 U.S.C. 315(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petitioner or real party in interest files a civil action challenging validity on or after the date the petitioner files a petition for IPR, that civil action shall be automatically stayed until specified events (patent owner moves to lift stay; patent owner files a civil action/counterclaim alleging infringement; or petitioner moves to dismiss).

rubrics_metrics.name: One‑year time bar after service of infringement complaint (35 U.S.C. 315(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An inter partes review may not be instituted if the petition is filed more than 1 year after the date on which the petitioner, real party in interest, or privy was served with a complaint alleging infringement of the patent. The time limitation does not apply to a request for joinder under 315(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder discretion (35 U.S.C. 315(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director institutes an IPR, the Director, in his or her discretion, may join as a party any person who properly files a petition under section 311 that the Director, after receiving a preliminary response or expiration of time for such response, determines warrants institution under section 314.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's authority over multiple proceedings (35 U.S.C. 315(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: During the pendency of an IPR, if another proceeding or matter involving the patent is before the Office, the Director may determine how the IPR or other proceeding may proceed, including providing for stay, transfer, consolidation, or termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel — Office proceedings (35 U.S.C. 315(e)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner (or real party in interest/privy) in an IPR that results in a final written decision may not request or maintain a proceeding before the Office with respect to that claim on any ground that the petitioner raised or reasonably could have raised during that IPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel — civil actions and ITC (35 U.S.C. 315(e)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner (or real party in interest/privy) in an IPR that results in a final written decision may not assert in a civil action under section 1338 or in an ITC proceeding under section 337 that the claim is invalid on any ground that the petitioner raised or reasonably could have raised during that IPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations on conduct of IPR (35 U.S.C. 316(a) selections)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall prescribe regulations providing that the file is public (subject to sealing), procedures for submission of supplemental information, governing relationship to other proceedings, discovery standards and limits, sanctions, protective orders, patent owner response after institution, standards for motions to amend, right to oral hearing, timing limits, joinder request periods, and petitioner comment opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights include limited discovery (depositions of affidavit/declaration witnesses and what is necessary in interest of justice); sanctions for abuse; protective orders for confidential info; requiring patent owner to file affidavits/declarations with its post‑institution response if relying on additional facts or expert opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations when prescribing regulations (35 U.S.C. 316(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In prescribing regulations, the Director shall consider the effect on the economy, integrity of the patent system, efficient administration of the Office, and ability to timely complete proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB conducts IPRs (35 U.S.C. 316(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Trial and Appeal Board, in accordance with section 6, shall conduct each inter partes review instituted under this chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner motion to amend — one motion, permitted remedies (35 U.S.C. 316(d)(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: During an IPR, the patent owner may file one motion to amend the patent to (A) cancel any challenged claim; and/or (B) for each challenged claim, propose a reasonable number of substitute claims. Additional motions may be permitted jointly or by regulation. An amendment may not enlarge the scope of the claims or introduce new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations set standards and procedures for allowing amendment and require information submitted in support to be made part of prosecution history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary standard in IPR (35 U.S.C. 316(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: In an inter partes review, the petitioner shall have the burden of proving a proposition of unpatentability by a preponderance of the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement and termination effects (35 U.S.C. 317(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: An IPR shall be terminated with respect to any petitioner upon joint request of the petitioner and patent owner unless the Office has decided the merits; termination under this section prevents estoppel under 315(e) from attaching to that petitioner. Any agreement or understanding in connection with termination must be in writing, filed, and may be treated as business confidential information upon showing of good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final written decision and certificate (35 U.S.C. 318(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If an IPR is instituted and not dismissed, the PTAB shall issue a final written decision on patentability of challenged claims and any new claim added. If final and appeal time expired, the Director shall issue and publish a certificate canceling claims finally determined unpatentable, confirming patentable claims, and incorporating any new/amended claims determined patentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervening rights for amended/new claims (35 U.S.C. 318(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amended or new claim determined patentable and incorporated after IPR shall have the same effect as specified in section 252 for reissued patents regarding rights of prior users/makers/importers or those who made substantial preparation before issuance of the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public data on length of reviews (35 U.S.C. 318(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office shall make available to the public data describing the length of time between institution and issuance of final written decision for each IPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to appeal PTAB final decisions (35 U.S.C. 319)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party dissatisfied with the PTAB final written decision may appeal pursuant to sections 141 through 144; any party to the IPR shall have the right to be a party to the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA inter partes reexamination requester eligibility and timing (35 U.S.C. 311 (pre-AIA))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any third‑party requester at any time may file a request for inter partes reexamination of a patent on the basis of any prior art cited under section 301 (applicable only to requests filed before Sept. 16, 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editor note: limited to pre‑AIA requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA request requirements — identity, fee, pertinency (35 U.S.C. 311(b) (pre-AIA))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must be in writing, include identity of real party in interest, be accompanied by payment of an inter partes reexamination fee, and set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director must promptly send a copy of the request to the owner of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional determination of reasonable likelihood within 3 months (35 U.S.C. 312(a) (transitional))
rubrics_metrics.description: Not later than 3 months after filing of a request for inter partes reexamination, the Director shall determine whether the information shows a reasonable likelihood that the requester would prevail with respect to at least one challenged claim, with or without consideration of other patents/printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A showing of reasonable likelihood is not precluded because a patent/printed publication was previously cited or considered by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order for inter partes reexamination if reasonable likelihood shown (35 U.S.C. 313 (transitional))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director finds reasonable likelihood that the requester would prevail with respect to at least one claim, the determination shall include an order for inter partes reexamination of the patent to resolve the question; the order may be accompanied by the Office's initial action on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of pre‑AIA inter partes reexamination — procedures and responses (35 U.S.C. 314 (pre-AIA))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination shall be conducted according to procedures for initial examination (sections 132 and 133). Patent owner may propose amendments and new claims (not enlarging scope). Documents filed by either party (except the request) shall be served on the other. Third‑party requester gets copies of Office communications and one opportunity to file written comments within 30 days after service of patent owner's response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special dispatch required unless Director provides otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special dispatch requirement for inter partes reexaminations (35 U.S.C. 314(c) (pre-AIA))
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise provided by the Director for good cause, all inter partes reexamination proceedings, including appeals, shall be conducted with special dispatch within the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA appeal rights and estoppel (35 U.S.C. 315 (pre-AIA))
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner and third‑party requester may appeal under section 134 and sections 141–144 as appropriate. A third‑party requester whose request results in an order is estopped from later asserting invalidity in civil action on any ground which it raised or could have raised during the reexamination, except newly discovered prior art unavailable at the time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA certificate of patentability/unpatentability (35 U.S.C. 316 (pre-AIA))
rubrics_metrics.description: When appeal time has expired or appeals terminated, the Director shall issue and publish a certificate canceling any claim finally determined unpatentable, confirming any claim determined patentable, and incorporating into the patent any amended or new claim determined patentable. Such amended/new claims have effect like section 252 for reissued patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA prohibition on successive requests after order (35 U.S.C. 317 (pre-AIA))
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an order for inter partes reexamination has been issued under section 313, neither the third‑party requester nor its privies may file a subsequent request for inter partes reexamination of the patent until an inter partes reexamination certificate is issued and published, unless authorized by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also bars requests on issues raised or which could have been raised in prior civil action or reexamination, subject to newly discovered prior art exception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIA stay of litigation upon reexamination order (35 U.S.C. 318 (pre-AIA))
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an order for inter partes reexamination of a patent has been issued, the patent owner may obtain a stay of any pending litigation involving an issue of patentability of claims subject to the reexamination order, unless the court finds a stay would not serve interests of justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑grant review applicability (35 U.S.C. 321 note & 321(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-grant review provisions of the AIA apply only to patents subject to the first-inventor-to-file provisions of the AIA, except as provided in AIA § 18 and limited transitional rules. The Director may impose a limit on the number of post-grant reviews instituted during each of the first four 1‑year periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file post‑grant review and fees (35 U.S.C. 321(2)(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the provisions of this chapter, a person who is not the owner of a patent may file with the Office a petition to institute a post-grant review of the patent. The Director shall establish, by regulation, fees to be paid by the person requesting the review in amounts the Director determines reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post‑grant review scope — grounds (35 U.S.C. 321(2)(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner in a post-grant review may request to cancel as unpatentable one or more claims of a patent on any ground that could be raised under paragraph (2) or (3) of section 282(b) (relating to invalidity of the patent or any claim).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing deadline for post‑grant review (35 U.S.C. 321(2)(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for a post-grant review may only be filed not later than 9 months after the date of the grant of the patent or of the issuance of a reissue patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition requirements for post‑grant review (35 U.S.C. 322(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition filed under section 321 may be considered only if the petition is accompanied by payment of the fee established by the Director and the petition identifies all real parties in interest (additional statutory requirements continue in the statute).
